candidate.family: exact finite-state activation-mask junction-tree message passing
candidate.purpose: model post-ReLU non-Gaussian dependence exactly via activation-cone mask state

structural_proof.factor_scope: for dense W_(l+1), every next-layer sign/moment factor touches every prior mask bit
structural_proof.reachability: if square W1 is full rank, x->W1 x is onto and every preactivation orthant/sign mask is feasible
structural_proof.scope_of_claim: lower bound applies to the frozen explicit finite-state mask-message estimator family, not all possible symbolic cone algorithms

blocker: Dense full-rank post-ReLU dependence destroys the separator compression needed by explicit finite-state mask message passing: the exact junction-tree bag is width 1024 and requires 2^1024 states, while the entire competition budget could support at most 38 binary bag bits even under the impossible optimistic cost of one FLOP per state.

interpretation.e111_connection: E111 showed moment-Gaussianization bias; E112 attempted to preserve the non-Gaussian mask dependence exactly instead of approximating it.
interpretation.result: Exact dependence representation is structurally correct but computationally inadmissible for dense width-1024 layers.
interpretation.next_search_constraint: A successor must compress non-Gaussian dependence without explicit full activation-mask state; viable mechanisms need a certified low-dimensional sufficient statistic, sparse conditional structure, or a controlled approximation/remainder bound.
